title: Organic Food: Is It Better for You?
summary: Cleveland Clinic dietitian explainer on what the organic label requires, its possible benefits, and its higher cost.

assertions.quote: Organic food is not necessarily pesticide-free
Only products that contain at least 95% organic ingredients can be certified organic and display the USDA seal.
Certified organic farms and food processors must be recertified every year
No antibiotics or growth hormones for livestock.
Livestock fed through grazing usually have higher levels of omega-3 fatty acids
Studies have shown significantly lower levels of the toxic metal cadmium in organic grains.
Organically grown fruits, vegetables and grains have higher amounts of vitamin C, vitamin E and carotenoids.
Reduced exposure to pesticides and insecticides. This is a significant benefit of organic produce and grains.
it’s not certain that eating organic foods will make a difference in one’s health
it costs more money to eat organic foods
Don’t get stuck on organic or conventional food
